question: Does complexity born in the archipelago incubator survive when poured into an open classic world?
sourceFile: index.html (unmodified throughout; git diff --stat verified empty before and after the study)
background: v1.39 added collisions: collideArrive(payload) spawns visitor creatures from {tag,cs:[{g,sg,br,bh}]} at the dish rim, founding new lineages (one newLineage() call per arrival), and logIv('collide',payload) makes it a logged, replay-valid intervention. Mate compatibility is hue-based (hueDist<40 degrees, index.html line ~1262), so the pour lets us test whether an archipelago-incubated lineage's structure (per prior study incubator-trials.json: refugia let eyed, multi-part bodies persist to 120 minutes) survives, spreads, or vanishes when dropped into an open, unstructured dish, and whether hue distance gates that outcome.

protocol.bootstrapVerified: viewport forced to 1280x720 before bootstrap; resize() -> R=334 confirmed (R===min(W,H)/2-26); worldReady/initCharts/paused=true bootstrap block run verbatim; versusSeeds/heirSeeds/dynasty/parentDish reset before every initWorld
protocol.sterileProtocolFollowed: every pour executed as logIv('collide',payload) immediately followed by collideArrive(payload) -- the exact shipped path (same code shelfPour() uses in-game) -- with payload.cs built from live donor creature data {g,sg,br,bh} (br rounded to 3 decimals via Array.from) captured strictly before the recipient's initWorld/pour; no creature array was ever hand-edited
protocol.executionNote: run as sequential chunked JS execs against persistent in-page state (window.__study, monkey-patched helpers) in the same browser tab for the entire study; step(1/60) called directly in wall-clock-budgeted loops (~25-27s per exec, well under the ~30s tool ceiling), never resetting state mid-run; each full recipient world's 60-minute post-pour phase happened to complete in a single exec call (10-20s of real time at population ~10-60)
protocol.donorPrep: initWorld('arch', seed) run up to 324000 steps (90 min), sampled every 16200 steps (4.5 min), stopping early the first sample where eyed>=3 OR branched>=3 (structure-crop-ready, per protocol); harvested up to 12 living creatures preferring sg.length>0 or any-segment eye>0.4, recording {g,sg,br,bh}; donor mean hue = mean hue of the harvested crop actually poured (not the whole donor population)
protocol.prep8400: for Arm 2's reverse pour: initWorld('classic', 8400+k) run exactly 36000 steps (10 min), then 12 living creatures harvested with NO structure preference ('plain classic natives') -- confirmed 0/12 had any body segments in every one of the 4 preps
protocol.recipientProtocol: initWorld(scenario, recipientSeed) -> run 36000 steps (10 min, establishes natives) -> pour -> run 216000 more steps (60 min), snapshot taken every 10800 steps (3 min) ALIGNED TO THE POUR STEP (not to absolute step 0), so checkpoints land exactly at pour+3,+6,+9,...,+60 minutes

fieldDefinitions.pop: creatures.length (living only; the engine compacts dead creatures out of the array every step)
fieldDefinitions.withParts: creatures with sg.length>0 (>=1 body segment beyond the base body)
fieldDefinitions.branched: withParts creatures where some segment o has o.par!==index-1 OR o.ang!==0 -- the game's own 'first branch' detection logic (index.html ~line 2139); note this triggers on a single angled appendage, not only true Y-forks
fieldDefinitions.eyed: creatures with a segment where o.eye>0.4 (checked independently of branched/paddler status)
fieldDefinitions.paddlers: creatures with a segment where o.ang!==0 AND o.fin>0.5
fieldDefinitions.maxParts: max sg.length among living creatures at sample time
fieldDefinitions.visitorLineagePop: count of living creatures whose .lin is EXACTLY one of the lineage ids created by collideArrive at this pour (captured via linNext diff before/after collideArrive). Strict: a visitor's own descendant that has drifted hue far enough to found a NEW sub-lineage (lineageOf() hue drift >30 degrees from founding hue) is NOT counted here even though it is visitor-descended -- this is a conservative, exact-label proxy, not a full pedigree.
fieldDefinitions.hybridsCumulative: cumulative count, since this replicate's pour, of sexual-reproduction events whose two parents have exactly one of {mother,father} with .lin in the visitor-arrival set (XOR). Captured by a non-invasive runtime observer wrapped around segInherit/makeCreature/applySegs: pure pass-through wrappers that record parent identity via array-reference lookup and call straight through to the original, unmodified functions -- zero RNG consumption, zero change to simulation state or outcome, verified deterministic. Same strict-lineage-id caveat as visitorLineagePop applies (undercounts once a lineage sub-forks).

protocol.instrumentationCaveat: Because visitorLineagePop and hybridsCumulative both use the STRICT arrival-lineage-id set, they undercount true visitor ancestry once hue drift forks a new sub-lineage or once admixed genes are carried by a creature now labeled with a native lineage id. The raw eyed/branched/withParts/maxParts counts are population-wide (not lineage-gated) and can include native-only convergent structure. The two views are complementary and both reported; neither alone cleanly isolates 'visitor-caused' structure from 'the recipient world's own tendency to sprout structure' (per this project's own crown-and-replication.json finding that classic worlds sometimes do this unaided).

arm1_islandToMainland.design: initWorld('classic', 8200+k) -> 10min native establishment -> pour donor k's archipelago crop -> 60min tracked

arm2_reversePour.design: initWorld('arch', 8300+k) -> 10min native establishment -> pour 12 plain classic natives (prep8400 8400+k) -> 60min tracked. Tests whether plain mainland bodies dilute the archipelago nursery's structure-preserving tendency.

arm3_hueControl.design: repeats Arm 1's recipient protocol at a NEW recipient seed (8500+k) using the SAME donor crop as the matching Arm 1 replicate; classifies each replicate by circular hue distance (engine's own hueDist()) between donor-crop mean hue and recipient native mean hue at the pre-pour moment: HYBRIDIZING if gap<40 degrees (matches the mate-compatibility gate), INVASIVE if gap>60 degrees, else AMBIGUOUS. Natural seed-driven hues produced 3 HYBRIDIZING (gap 33.65, 34.37, 36.83) and 1 INVASIVE (gap 76.53) without any forcing.

summary.visitorLineageSurvivedTo60min: 0/12 (strict arrival-lineage-id definition; every replicate's original visitor label went extinct before +60min, range +3min to +51min)
summary.trueEyeSurvivedTo60min_populationWide: 0/12 (NOT ONE of the 12 recipient worlds had a real eye, eye>0.4, present at the exact +60min checkpoint, despite transient peaks up to 11 eyed creatures mid-run in several replicates)

verdict: Island lineage identity never survives the crossing: in all 12 recipient worlds, across all three arms, the strict visitor-arrival lineage label went extinct before the 60-minute mark (fastest: 3 minutes; slowest: 51 minutes; 0/12 survived to +60min). True eyes fared no better structurally: eye>0.4 creatures appeared transiently in 7 of the 12 replicates (peaking as high as 11 individuals in the one INVASIVE hue-control replicate at +18min), but in every single replicate that structure had collapsed back to zero eyed creatures by +60min -- island eyes are a peak, not an acquisition, exactly like the unaided classic-world runs in crown-and-replication.json. Coarser body structure (branched, the game's own forked-segment definition) fared better: 9 of 12 worlds still had some branched creatures at +60min, but because the strict visitor label is always extinct by then and hybrid births (2 to 189 per replicate, present in 11 of 12) mixed transplant genes into natively-labeled lineages before that extinction, this persistence cannot be cleanly credited to the transplant versus the recipient world's own independent tendency to sprout structure -- both views are reported rather than collapsed into one number. The reverse pour did not dilute the archipelago nursery: despite receiving a dozen genuinely featureless mainland bodies (0/12 parts in every one of the 4 prep crops) and heavy hybridization (15-189 cross-lineage births), Arm 2's archipelago recipients ended the hour with MORE population-wide branched structure on average (7.25 per replicate) than either classic-recipient arm (2.0 in Arm 1, 1.5 in Arm 3), and populations stayed within the archipelago's normal low-population range (9-15) rather than collapsing -- the refugia mechanism looks robust to a one-time demographic and genetic shock, though n=4 is directional, not conclusive. Hue distance strongly and cleanly gates GENE FLOW exactly as the mate-compatibility code predicts: the three HYBRIDIZING replicates (mean hue gap 34-37 degrees) produced 14 to 183 cross-lineage births each, while the one INVASIVE replicate (gap 76.5 degrees) produced only 4 -- a residual trickle explainable by individual hue variance around the population means rather than bulk interbreeding, since mate eligibility itself is gated at hueDist<40. Whether hue distance also changes STRUCTURAL survival specifically is not resolved here: with only one invasive replicate against three hybridizing ones, the single data point (which happened to show the largest transient eyed peak of the whole study, then the most total collapse -- zero parts, zero branches, zero eyes, lowest population -- by +60min) is suggestive but not a controlled comparison; it is flagged as a candidate for a dedicated, better-replicated follow-up rather than reported as a finding.
forThePaper: Pour a refugia-incubated lineage into an open dish and the label dies fast -- every one of twelve archipelago-to-mainland transplants lost its founding lineage identity within an hour, most within twenty minutes, and every transient burst of real eyes (up to eleven individuals at once, in one run) melted back to zero by the sixty-minute mark, echoing the same collapse this project already logged in unaided classic worlds. What crosses over is not the island population but its genes: cross-lineage hybrid births numbered in the dozens to low hundreds whenever donor and native hues sat within the engine's own forty-degree mate-compatibility window, and collapsed to a residual trickle of four when they didn't, confirming that the hue gate is doing real ecological work and not just cosmetic species-painting. And the nursery itself proved sturdy in reverse: pouring a dozen genuinely bodyless mainland natives into the archipelago -- and watching them interbreed by the hundreds -- left the refugia worlds with more branched structure at the hour mark than either classic-world arm managed on its own, suggesting the geography that lets local extinction fuel invention (per refugia-sweep.json) survives a one-time demographic flood better than any single lineage survives leaving home.
